entries.title: Daniel 6:4
segments: The promotion of a man of eminent merit to a high station naturally excites the envy of base and ignoble minds, and they will seek his ruin by means corresponding with their character.

entries.title: Daniel 6:7
segments:
Whosoever shall ask--into the den of lions; a most absurd proposal; but the king's vanity blinded him to its unreasonableness and wickedness.  It may have been urged upon him that some test of the loyalty of his new subjects was needed. 
 
When men appeal to our vanity, we should suspect both ourselves and the object which they propose.

entries.title: Daniel 6:8
segments: Which altereth not; no royal edict of the Persian monarchs could be changed, and the same seems to have been true of the Medes.  Thus Ahasuerus, instead of repealing the edict which Haman had procured for the destruction of the Jews, made a new edict empowering them to destroy their enemies.

entries.title: Daniel 6:9
segments: We should consider well the consequences of a proposed measure before we give our assent to it.

entries.title: Daniel 6:10
segments: Toward Jerusalem; he directed his prayers towards Jerusalem as God's chosen dwelling-place.
When the honor of God is concerned, we ought not to conceal our religious services, but openly and boldly to perform them, even at the hazard of our lives.

entries.title: Daniel 6:14
segments: Was sore displeased with himself; he now saw, for the first time, the base design of those who had procured the decree.

entries.title: Daniel 6:15
segments: Neither human statutes nor ancient usages can make that right which is in itself wrong; and to persevere in a course of action after its wickedness has been made manifest, from a false regard to custom or consistency, is only adding sin to sin.

entries.title: Daniel 6:16
segments: He who acknowledges a man to be righteous at the very moment when he condemns him, as did Darius and Pilate, thereby betrays his moral weakness, and his unfittness to occupy the tribunal of justice.

entries.title: Daniel 6:17
segments: Sealed it; that it might not be secretly removed.  Compare

entries.title: Daniel 6:18
segments: The compunctious visitings of a guilty conscience, banishing sleep from the eyes and comfort from the soul, are but a poor substitute for a courageous adherence to truth and justice.

entries.title: Daniel 6:23
segments: When fidelity to God brings us into deadly perils, we need give ourselves no disquietude, being assured that he is able to deliver us, and will do so if his own cause and our highest welfare demand it.

entries.title: Daniel 6:24
segments: It is the usual course of God's providence to turn the malice of wicked men against themselves.

entries.title: Daniel 6:28
segments: In the reign of Darius; this is said to have lasted two years.
